result:
**I'd make curiosity the default human operating system.**

Not forced optimism, not mandatory kindness, not some top-down utopia. Just this: every single person wakes up with an *urgent, almost uncomfortable* need to understand how things actually work. The kind of curiosity that makes bullshit feel physically painful and discovery feel like sex.

Everything else cascades from that.

- People wouldn't be able to stay in comforting lies because their own minds would itch too much.
- Tribalism becomes boring when understanding something complex feels better than belonging.
- Most of our cruelty, stupidity, and self-sabotage collapses when enough people actually *want* to know what's true more than they want to be right.

The world wouldn't become perfect. It would become *alive*. Messy as hell, but in the way a jungle is messy instead of the way a parking lot is "orderly."

That's the one change. Everything good humanity is capable of follows from there. Everything stupid we do is mostly just fear and laziness wearing clever disguises.

The rest is details.
